title: The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A publicist can operate as institutional infrastructure by deciding what becomes legible, to whom, through which relationships and records—but narrative power must be governed through evidence, approvals, credit, access, correction, and ethical limits.
The image is a distinct authored work around fashion; the clothes, staging, model, commission, publication, and photograph do not collapse into one ownership question.
narrativeSequence.rights: Free to Use and Reuse / Library of Congress curated set

narrativeSequence.caption: 01 · FRAME — What is the house asking the public to understand?. Write the evidenced proposition, intended audience, context, proof, exclusions, affected people, and correction condition. Separate a useful frame from a claim the available record cannot support.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · RELATE — Which relationships carry the frame?. Map journalists, editors, critics, stylists, talent, institutions, buyers, creators, community authorities, platforms, and internal spokespeople. Record the purpose, relevant disclosure, access terms, embargo, conflicts, and who is excluded.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · GOVERN — Who may say, approve, reuse, and retain what?. Define scope of services, spokesperson authority, substantiation, review time, confidential information, identity and image permissions, media and territory, archive copies, post-term use, credit, correction, takedown, and termination from the actual agreement.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · REMEMBER — What enters the institutional record?. Preserve final releases, pitches where appropriate, media lists under proper privacy controls, approvals, corrections, placements, refusals, captions, credits, rights evidence, and decision context. The archive should record how public meaning was made—not only the resulting coverage.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Take one launch and list every public claim, its evidence, approver, spokesperson, audience, channel, and correction trigger.
Map every relationship carrying the story, including access, embargo, compensation or material connection, conflict, exclusion, and disclosure.
Bind every image, quote, name, biography, product claim, and archive use to an exact permission or review status.
After coverage, archive placements, refusals, errors, corrections, audience questions, and what the house learned—not just reach.
